server.name: Corsair Cloud
server.title: Corsair Cloud
server.description: Access and run actions across your connected apps.

protocolMetadata.instructions: Corsair connects this agent to the user's own apps. Start with list_integrations to see what is connected here, and list_integration_operations to get an operation's exact arguments before calling it. run_script performs work now; add_triggers performs it later, whenever an integration sends a matching event. If an integration is missing or unconnected, add_integrations returns a link for the user to authorize it — hand them that link rather than retrying. After adding a trigger, list_runs is how you learn whether it fired and whether the action worked; a trigger that registered cleanly can still fail on its first real event.

tool.name: add_triggers
tool.title: Add a trigger
tool.description: Run JavaScript whenever an integration sends a matching event. `trigger` says what to watch; `action` is the body to run, in the same dialect as run_script, with `corsair` and the event as `payload` in scope. Narrow with `trigger.equals` so it fires on the events you mean — without it, every event from that integration runs the action. Check argument names with list_integration_operations first: the action is compiled when it is saved, and an operation Corsair does not know is refused.

name.description: A name for the workflow this creates. Defaults to what it watches.

action.description: JavaScript to run when the event matches. A function body: `corsair` and `payload` (the event) are in scope. e.g. `await corsair.slack.api.chat.postMessage({ channel: "C1", text: payload.data.title });`

event.description: The event name to match, e.g. 'Issue.update'. Omit to run on every event this integration sends.

equals.description: Event paths that must match exactly, ANDed, e.g. {"data.state.name": "Done"}. The event body is under `data`.

integration.description: The integration whose events to watch, e.g. 'linear'.

trigger.description: What has to happen for the action to run.

tool.name: run_script
tool.title: Run a script now
tool.description: Run a JavaScript snippet against this tenant's Corsair. The snippet is an async function BODY: `return` your result. The only thing in scope is the global `corsair` — call operations as `await corsair.<plugin>.api.<op>(args)` (e.g. `await corsair.slack.api.channels.list({})`) and use ordinary JS (filter/map/loops) to combine them. Use list_integration_operations to discover paths and arguments. No network, filesystem, process, require, or imports are available — only corsair operations.

_published_faq.name: How do I add Corsair Cloud to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Add Corsair Cloud to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor by connecting its remote MCP URL in each client's MCP settings. In Claude, add a custom connector. In ChatGPT, add an MCP app. In Cursor, add an MCP server under Settings. The MCP URL is https://mcp.corsair.cloud/projsvjx3pghd5e/mcpg_pVYMClULrdy2Nr0yEHRx2dMZLc3KlJmi/mcp.

_published_faq.name: Is Corsair Cloud MCP ready for ChatGPT and Claude?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 17, 2026, Corsair Cloud scores 94/100 on Manufact's MCP publishing checklist. The scan does not yet meet ChatGPT publishing checks and meets Claude publishing checks. Passing these checks does not guarantee marketplace approval.

_published_faq.name: How clear is Corsair Cloud's MCP tool documentation?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 17, 2026, Corsair Cloud scores 87/100 in Manufact's review of tool titles, descriptions, input and output schemas, and behavior annotations. The review covers 9 of 9 discovered tools. The quality score measures documentation clarity; runtime behavior and marketplace readiness require separate checks.

_published_faq.name: What are the best alternatives to Corsair Cloud?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 17, 2026, alternatives to Corsair Cloud in automation-workflows on the Manufact MCP catalog include Sidewave Maggiordomo, Fleet Workspace, Whalesync, typenode-mcp, and tinyfish.

_published_faq.name: How can Corsair Cloud improve its MCP documentation?

acceptedAnswer.text: run_script is the lowest-scoring reviewed tool at 76/100. Declare the result fields and their types in the output schema. Open its review for feedback and a copyable fix prompt, then rerun the documentation review after updating your tool metadata.
